Equal Ability Bill
Equal Ability Bill

Recognizing the need to extend social benefits to all citizens, the Grand National Assembly has approved the Equal Ability Bill (E.A.B.). Section I of the E.A.B. proposes an amendment to the 1933 compensatory veterans and state employees' disability benefits program. The amendment expands Subsection III to include an earnings replacement benefit applicable to all non-state employed citizens. Under this newly expanded program, any employees who suffer severe illness or become disabled, thereby losing their capacity to work, will be provided a steady income by the state. This income will be set at 50% of their monthly salary, ensuring a measure of financial security for these citizens in their time of need. [-1 Government Budget]
The EABA bill has been passed by the GNA.
Security Act
Security Act

In response to the heightened need for security due to the ongoing social unrest, the Grand National Assembly (GNA) presents the Security Act (S.A.) to fortify public safety measures.

Section I of the S.A. grants security forces the discretion to use force as deemed necessary to uphold law and order. This provision is designed to enable quick and decisive responses in situations where public safety is at risk.

Section II of the S.A. authorizes suspicion-based arrests and confiscations without the prerequisite of a warrant. This measure seeks to expedite law enforcement's response to potential threats, thereby enhancing overall security.

Section III of the S.A. allows security forces to exercise their authority beyond standard legal limits if such action is deemed essential for maintaining state security and protecting the general public. This clause reinforces the commitment to safeguarding national security and upholding public safety in the face of increasing unrest.
A SA bill has been passed by the GNA.
The Bergia Autonomy and Local Governance Act
The Bergia Autonomy and Local Governance Act

The Bergia Autonomy and Local Governance Act, otherwise known as the BALGA, sets forth the framework for an autonomous governance system in Bergia, promoting regional autonomy and stronger local representation. The Grand National Assembly passes the following actions:

Section I sanctions the election of a local governor. This measure ensures that the people of Bergia have direct representation and decision-making power in their regional affairs.

Section II calls for the replacement of the current special zone laws with a democratic system that respects and promotes local interests. This action fortifies the principle of local representation with the formation of a Bergian Regional Assembly and gives the region its due autonomy.

Section III underlines the establishment of 'Bergia Semi-Autonomous Region' as a symbol of local autonomy and democratic representation, fostering a fresh era of localized governance.
The BALGA bill has been passed by the GNA.
The Bergia Standardization and Unity Measure
The Bergia Standardization and Unity Measure

The Bergia Standardization and Unity Measure, dubbed as the BSUM, outlines the course for the full integration of Bergia into national governance, advocating for uniformity in governance and a reinforced sense of national unity. The Grand National Assembly passes the following steps: Section I endorses the abolishment of the governor's position, transitioning to mayoral elections within each city. This change aligns Bergia's local governance with the rest of the nation, fostering a sense of unity and national integration. Section II calls for the total revocation of the special zone, abolishment of the position of governor, and dissolving the local security forces. With these measures, Bergia can finally be an equal part of Sordland. Section III promotes the enforcement of standard national laws and policies across Bergia, dismantling the current semi-independent security structure. The security of the region will henceforth be under the full control of the Ministry of the Interior, curtailing any unaccountable violence. [-1 Government Budget]
The BSUM bill has been passed by the GNA.

ATO Supports the Bergia Autonomous Zone in Sordland

The ATO extends its full support for the establishment of the Autonomous Zone of Bergia in Sordland. This initiative provides the Bludish minority with local autonomy, allowing them to preserve and promote their cultural heritage. The ATO recognizes this step as an important advancement in fostering inclusivity and safeguarding minority rights.

The creation of the Bergia Special Zone represents a strategic effort to promote social harmony and mutual respect among Sordland's diverse population. It reflects the government’s dedication to ensuring equal rights and freedoms for all citizens, regardless of their ethnic or cultural background.

The ATO is confident that this initiative will contribute to long-term stability and peace in the region and views it as a constructive approach to addressing diversity within Sordland’s society.
Concerns Of Threats to Free Market Principles

Sordland's recent initiative to centralize its central bank has sparked controversy within ATO circles. Such a move, the alliance fears, could lead to a significant shift away from free-market principles, potentially hampering competition, stifling financial innovation, and ultimately leading to an undesirable concentration of financial power in the hands of the state. 

While the ATO acknowledges the need for effective financial regulation, it argues that excessive centralization could undermine the very pillars of a free and dynamic economy. The alliance therefore urges Sordland to adopt a more balanced approach, one that harmonizes state oversight with market-driven principles.
ATO Expresses Discontent Over Sordland-Valgsland Pact

In particular, Arcasian President Dwight Walker, representing the ATO's concerns, has drawn attention to Valgsland's enhanced naval activities in the Merkopa Sea. This naval escalation, coupled with the establishment of the new Sordland-Valgsland alliance, is perceived as a potential source of regional destabilization. Consequently, the ATO, and by extension, Arcasia, is urging restraint in the face of these shifting geopolitical dynamics.

The alliance emphasized that the right to self-defense is an essential component of personal liberty, aligning with the principles upheld by its member states.

The military industry, reflecting the alliance's perspective, has welcomed this decision as a reinforcement of individual rights and freedoms. The ATO regards this landmark move as a vital measure to strengthen the foundations of personal liberty and contribute to the resilience of a free and secure society.

The alliance perceives this move as a potential infringement on the fundamental freedoms of expression and religion. The ATO argues that such restrictions could undermine cultural diversity, infringe upon personal liberties, and foster social discord. 

Consequently, the alliance calls upon Sordland to reconsider this decree, emphasizing the need to harmonize national security concerns with the upholding of fundamental rights and freedoms.

Framing such measures as outdated, the CSP emphasized the need for criminal justice systems to evolve in ways that reflect the principles of equity and fairness in modern society.

Chairman Leon "Malenyev" Chavatangakwunua, representing the CSP's stance, warns of the potential for this strategic alliance to disrupt the delicate equilibrium of power in the region.

The CSP believes that the establishment of the Bergia Autonomous Zone might inadvertently provide a platform for such groups to exert their influence, which could lead to heightened tensions and potential conflicts. The CSP has called upon the international community to carefully monitor the unfolding situation and act proactively to prevent any escalation.

It insists that the privatization of prisons could compromise inmates' rights, and impede the nation's pursuit of social justice. The alliance, therefore, encourages Sordland to reconsider this policy, emphasizing the fundamental role of the state in administering justice.

The CSP's approach differs markedly from that of the ATO, with its emphasis on preventative measures such as border security and travel restrictions. Instead, the CSP champions the deployment of a large-scale vaccination campaign to contain the outbreak at its source. During the meeting, the CSP also stressed the need for unified action, resource mobilization, and collaborative efforts between member nations to effectively manage and mitigate the health crisis.

Summer of Love

Smokes Taxed

Health officials around the country have praised the discouragement of Tobacco with the increased taxes.

BFF Terror And Government Incoordination Claim Innocent Lives

NFP To Get What’s Coming To Them?

Will an investigation by Anton Rayne’s new Anti-Corruption Police finally be the undoing of the National Front party? For years, we’ve suspected that Kesaro Kibener’s band of nationalist thugs have been involved in all kinds of shady business. Now, thanks to insider reports hinting at ties to the Bernard Circas assassination, we know that at least some of our suspicions can be confirmed. Sordland will be a lot safer once key NFP members are behind bars.
Zone of Oppression and Racism in Bergia

The Maroon Palace has shown their racist and totalist colors by creating a special zone for Bergia where parallel laws of more oppression and racism exist for the governor to use. The Rayne administration only has the tool that is the hammer and fiend itself seeing all the problems as nails. Violence creates more violence, hate creates more hate. This zone will raise a generation of freedom fighters.

President Rayne has unleashed a chain of events that he is not fully aware of. The future generations will suffer for decades while the people alive now will experience the tragedy of division and hatred.
Winds of Change at Capitol Park

We had enough! It’s been two days since we gathered together in the Capitol Park to demand answers from the government! We will stay here two years if need be.

Even in a peaceful rally like this, the extreme police presence is a testament to the administration's views on exercising our democratic rights. If we don’t protect our rights then no one will.

Time is now! Come and join us, brothers and sisters! Ride the winds of change and come to Capitol Park!
The Fall of Hawker: Chief Justice Falls Victim To The Senseless Violence He Once Promoted

In a twist of fate that has left many with mixed emotions, Chief Justice Orso Hawker, a divisive figure known for his controversial decisions and unwavering support of oppressive systems, has met a tragic end in the streets of Holsord. Disability Bill to Offer Safety Net

After a very long period of heated discussions, the Grand National Assembly has passed an expansion to the existing 1933 veteran and state employee program, allowing private-sector employees to claim a portion of their salary in the case of falling sick and gravely ill. The bill that was approved by the government ensures the unlucky in our society has a chance to continue living without falling below the poverty line.

The government must be praised for this decision to extend the social safety nets of our society. Under the new law, the employee incapable of working will be given 50% of their last salary every month until they recover and are able to work again. The bill that was rejected by the government would ensure that the unlucky in our society had a chance to continue living without falling below the poverty line. However, thanks to Rayne that is not the case.

Anton Rayne Donates To Support Women. Will Policies Follow?

FC Anrica and FC Gelsord Hand in Hand

For the only time in their history, the sworn rivals FC Anrica and FC Gelsord fans stood side by side against the police brutality. During the derby match yesterday, the fans of both teams united to protest the security forces mishandling of the recent events.

President Sends Dimwit Son To Arcasia

Following rumors that young Franc Rayne had failed his university exams, we were disappointed -- but sadly not surprised -- to learn that the President’s son will be attending Harcard University, the most prestigious and expensive school in Arcasia. Governor Bron Continues His Racist Policies

We condemn Governor Bron's callousness and demand an immediate end to these reprehensible policies.

According to reports on the ground, the wider Bludish community is getting restless about the ongoing discrimination and are increasingly organizing rallies around the region despite the governor's harsh and often violent reactions. We salute the Bludish community and their fight for equality.
Governor Ersen Nullifies Racist Laws

Orso Hawker’s Death Raises Eyebrows

Brotherhood of the People

Coward!

Kibener Passed!

Kesaro Kibener has always been a controversial figure. He has worked years and years to segregate Sordish people from Bludish. It looks like his anti-Bludish sentiments and campaigns have finally paid off. Except for the price this time was his life.

Workers Tossed Pennies While Profiteers Thrive

With the economy cracking and families pushed into poverty, the government chooses to do nothing while clinging to broken theories. “Self-correction” is code for letting the rich survive while the rest suffer and starve. This is cruelty by design, cloaked in economic jargon.
New Office Tracks Collapse While Workers Wait

Spy Scandal Reveals Depths of Rayne Incompetence

De-Sollinization: Finally!

This move relieves the slight burden that was felt more on the backs of the working-class. The administration has done a great service to the people through this action and we hope that many more acts of state support come for welfare. Free healthcare for every Sordish citizen is within reach now.
Throwing Gasoline on a Fire

So what is the solution? Let’s just give everyone a rifle. What does President Rayne think this will solve?

Undoubtedly this was a move to protect himself and his seat. But, at the same time, there is nothing to do but welcome it as a way to lessen the great influence these generals have over our country.
Forced Relocation

Complex problems require complex solutions. Period. This administration continues to show that they don’t have the capacity to approach the complex problem of increasing education and health services in rural areas. President Rayne’s solution to this was dead simple.

Give the ‘servant’ in civil ‘servant’ a new meaning. Let’s just relocate our entire teaching and health staff to the rural areas, right? That will fix it. Why did we never think of this before? Here is another question. What happened to the rights of these teachers and doctors?
The President Removes Symbols of Oppression and Division

With his presidential power, the president has decided to remove all religious symbols from public places. In short, the president has finally decided to fight for what is right and remove symbols of oppression and division caused by the difference in one belief.
